about: HELL palette mode ('Lava', candidate C of the owner's mock-ups, retuned after play so cool greys and dull teals take the 2-2 column golds: tune candidate D): each 9-bit PC Engine colour (GGG RRR BBB) is sorted into a family by its HSV hue, saturation and value (channels 0-7 scaled to 0-1, hue in degrees) and re-coloured from that family's ramp. Grey or white (saturation below sat_low): 'ash' if value >= ash_v, else 'grey'. Otherwise 'steel' (cool neutrals: stone, walls, floors) if the colour fits any steel_windows entry [hue_lo, hue_hi, max_saturation, max_chroma, max_value] (hue_lo <= hue <= hue_hi, saturation <= max_saturation, saturation * value <= max_chroma, value <= max_value); else 'blue' if blue_hue[0] <= hue <= blue_hue[1], 'green' if green_hue[0] <= hue < green_hue[1], else 'warm'. Ramps are [position, R, G, B] points (channels 0-7) interpolated linearly at: blue = value * lava_mix[0] + luma * lava_mix[1], green = luma * green_luma_scale, grey = value, ash = (value - ash_v) / (1 - ash_v), steel = value * steel_mix[0] + luma * steel_mix[1]; luma = R * luma[0] + G * luma[1] + B * luma[2] (0-1). Warm colours keep their hue when it is <= warm_keep_hue[0] or >= warm_keep_hue[1], else take warm_other_hue; hues from warm_magenta[0] up to warm_magenta[1] become warm_magenta[1]; saturation is multiplied by warm_s and value by warm_v. Colour 0 (black) stays black. Results round to 3 bits a channel. The mode recolours background palettes 0-14 (VCE entries 0-239) only; the HUD palette and the sprite palettes keep their colours. scripts/palette_tables.py turns this file into the 512-entry table at build time. One stage may override one low-half colour (stage_overrides: {stage: {"$colour": [R, G, B]}}, the stage as Level Select numbers it): in 1-1, $094 (a sidewalk fleck and the skyline's shadow faces, crimson 601 in the table for 2-2's far ridge) shows 210, the dark gold-brown of 2-2's columns; the upload compares the key in that stage only.
